_experiment.description: Magnitude-based search criterion with the same manifold adjust step. Instead of selecting the weight that minimises d_W(og_net, pruned_net) at each step, select the weight with the smallest absolute value |w_ij|. The adjust step remains identical. Any difference in the sparsity curve between this and the baseline is attributable solely to the choice of search criterion: manifold distance minimisation vs magnitude heuristic. This is the core ablation for the thesis's central claim that d_W is a better pruning criterion than magnitude. NOTE: requires code change — add search field handling to prune() in sparsifier.py.
literature: Blalock et al. 2020 (survey): magnitude pruning is shown to be surprisingly competitive when paired with fine-tuning — this experiment checks whether the same holds when paired with the manifold adjust step instead of retraining
Molchanov et al. 2019 (importance estimation): systematic comparison of magnitude, first-order Taylor, and second-order importance metrics — this experiment adds the d_W criterion to that comparison
